seo.title: Multiples of 8 Speed Grid - 8s Times Tables Math Clicker
seo.metaDescription: Find all multiples of 8 on a 100-number grid. Boost 8-times table multiplication facts speed and accuracy for elementary learners.
seo.intro: Multiplying by 8 can be conceived as doubling a number three consecutive times (double, double, and double again). All multiples of 8 are even numbers that end in 8, 6, 4, 2, or 0 in a predictable repeating cycle. In this speed clicker, students locate all 12 multiples of 8 from 8 to 96 on the hundreds board. Fluency Development: When students engage in timed identification on a 100-number grid, they move beyond manual finger-counting and transition into visual pattern synthesis. Developing automaticity with this specific math concept reduces cognitive load during multi-step problem solving, long division, and algebraic equation manipulation.
seo.howToPlay: Click all multiples of 8 on the grid. Correct clicks turn green with a checkmark. Distractor clicks flash red with an X and deduct 2 seconds from your time. Spot all 12 multiples before the countdown hits zero. Keyboard and Accessibility Controls: Students can use a touchscreen, trackpad, mouse, or keyboard arrow keys to navigate between tiles. Pressing Space or Enter activates the focused tile. Wrong clicks temporarily flash red with an X icon and subtract 2 seconds, but remain unlocked so learners can self-correct without getting stuck.
seo.teacherNotes: Encourage the double-double-double mental strategy: for 8 x 6, double 6 to 12, double 12 to 24, and double 24 to 48. Classroom Implementation Ideas: Use this interactive grid during the first five minutes of math instruction as an energetic bell-ringer or daily warm-up. Teachers can project the screen onto an interactive whiteboard for whole-class competitive rounds, or assign the canonical link directly into Google Classroom for independent Chromebook math station rotations.

faq.q: What is the pattern of the last digits in multiples of 8?
faq.a: The ones digits follow a repeating cycle: 8, 6, 4, 2, 0, then 8, 6, 4, 2, 0 again.

faq.q: What is the largest multiple of 8 under 100?
faq.a: The largest multiple of 8 up to 100 is 96 (8 x 12 = 96).

faq.q: How does mastering click all multiples of 8 support higher-level math standards?
faq.a: Building speed and accuracy with click all multiples of 8 directly strengthens mental arithmetic and numerical reasoning. When foundational number facts become second nature, students can dedicate their active working memory to advanced problem-solving strategies, fraction equivalence, and multi-step word problems.
